game: IND@TEN Week 3 2025, kickoff 2025-09-21 13:00 ET, TEN +6, total 43.5, outdoor (forecast not saved; rest/travel and open-to-close move not in pack)

script.base: Market has IND leading a moderate game (implied IND 24.8, TEN 18.8). Base script: IND leans on Jonathan Taylor (43 carries, 236 rush yards in weeks 1-2) against a TEN run defense allowing 6.04 YPC and 9 runs of 10+, leads by about a score into the second half, and keeps handing him the ball late. TEN, already without LT JC Latham, trails and has to throw with Cam Ward rather than live on Tony Pollard (38 carries, 152 yards). Total 43.5 is not a shootout and not a slog.
script.flip1: IND gets up big early, milks the clock, Taylor's carries rise further while Michael Pittman, Tyler Warren and Alec Pierce routes stall, and TEN abandons the run so Calvin Ridley (14 targets) and Elic Ayomanor (13 targets, 202 air yards) see volume but Ward's -0.91 EPA/dropback vs the blitz and a backup left tackle cap the yards.
script.flip2: TEN hangs around or leads, IND cannot sit on the run, Taylor's rush line dies the way his 71-yard week already showed is possible, and both passing games stay live. A second, untestable flip is outdoor weather dragging the 43.5 total down; no forecast was saved.

injury_fallout: Sources: pack official pre-game injury report plus weeks 1-2 touches. TEN DT T'Vondre Sweat is Out (ankle), so IND's interior run (Taylor 43/236, Daniel Jones 13/28, DJ Giddens 12/41) faces a backup tackle; no replacement is named. TEN T JC Latham is Out (hip) and G Kevin Zeitler is Questionable (biceps), so Ward pressure should rise, TEN rush efficiency should fall, and quick throws (Chig Okonkwo 10 targets/30 air yards, Pollard 2 targets) are the outlet while deep yards for Ridley (140 air) and Ayomanor (202 air) are at risk. TEN S Kevin Winston Jr. is Doubtful (hamstring), which would help IND deep shots (Pierce 8 targets, 141 air, 104 yards) if he sits; TEN CBs L'Jarius Sneed (back) and Jarvis Brownlee Jr. (ankle) are only Questionable, so do not treat the secondary as confirmed backups. IND CB Charvarius Ward is Questionable (concussion); if he sits, Ridley/Ayomanor gain and that is unconfirmed. IND TE Tyler Warren is Questionable (toe) despite being the target leader (16 targets, 155 yards, 102 air); if limited, Pittman (13/120), Josh Downs (11/63), Pierce (8/104) and Taylor (5 targets, 77 rec yards) absorb, and Warren's 77.5 line has no margin (76 and 79). TEN WR Bryce Oliver (knee) is not in the target table. TEN RB Kalel Mullings is Questionable (ankle); if out, Pollard keeps the carries and Julius Chestnut (2 carries, 2 yards) is not a real pivot. Final inactives (~90 min pre-kick) are not in the pack.

matchup.pressure: TEN blitzes 29%; IND EPA/dropback is 0.29 vs blitz and 0.39 unblitzed, so IND is fine when blitzed and slightly better clean. IND blitzes 37%; TEN EPA/dropback is -0.91 vs blitz and -0.07 clean, so Ward is a problem when IND brings pressure, worsened by Latham Out.
matchup.bleeds: TEN run defense bleeds: 6.04 YPC, 9 runs of 10+ in two games, and middle YPA 7.93 (15 throws) vs left 6.68 (31) and right 5.48 (27); they also allowed 7 passes of 20+ for 75 yards. IND run defense allows 5.44 YPC and 6 runs of 10+; pass defense is tighter on explosives (3 of 20+ for 64) but bleeds left (8.18 YPA on 22) vs middle 5.22 (9) and right 4.17 (30).
matchup.overlap: Cleanest overlap is Taylor's carry share into TEN's 6.04 YPC run bleed with Sweat out, in a favorite script. Second overlap would be Warren into the middle (7.93 YPA) but he is Questionable and priced on his exact output. IND's left-side bleed (8.18) is a possible Ridley/Ayomanor spot, but alignment is unknown and IND's blitz plus Latham Out fights deep efficiency.

Warren 76 and 79 on 16 targets. Pittman 80 and 40. Pierce 36 and 68. Downs 12 and 51. Giddens rush 41 and 0. Pollard rush 60 and 92 (4.0 YPC on 152/38), rush+rec 89 and 92, rec 29 and 0. Ridley 27 and 57 on 14 targets/84 yards (6.0 per target). Ayomanor 13 and 56 on 13 targets/69 yards/202 air. Okonkwo 19 and 35. Dike 0 and -1 on 6 targets. Chestnut 2 rush yards. Role is stable: Taylor and Pollard are the only real rush shares; Warren is IND's top target; Ridley/Ayomanor are TEN's volume WRs without the efficiency.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Jonathan Taylor is the bellcow (43 carries, 236 yards, 5.5 YPC) for a 6-point favorite against a TEN run defense allowing 6.04 YPC and 9 runs of 10+ with DT T'Vondre Sweat out, so volume and efficiency both lean over a 118.5 line that only copies his two-game mean.
edge_players.must_be_true: Taylor plays a full snap/carry share near the 21.5 carries per game he has had; IND leads or stays on schedule so the run stays live; Sweat stays out.
edge_players.kills_it: IND falls behind and abandons the run (he already had a 71-yard week); Giddens (12 carries, a 41-yard game) or Jones (13/28) steals the extra work; TEN loads the box and the median-priced 118.5 holds.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and Taylor under 118.5 lost the ticket because the 165-yard week was the fluky one, TEN sold out to the box after two weeks of film, the unnamed Sweat replacement played fine, and Giddens or Jones took 10-plus touches in a game that stayed closer than -6. His other week was already 71, the line is the two-game mean not a discount, and with no no-vig we may simply be betting a fair number. That counter is real enough to keep this a lean and a flag, not strong enough to kill the stacked matchup (6.04 YPC, 9 explosive runs, DT out, favorite script, 43-carry role).
